scope: Theorem 6.3 (Unique Games input) of the manuscript “The Gaussian propeller bound in every dimension” (preprints/The-Gaussian-Propeller-Bound-in-Every-Dimension-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 096 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b546ae5fd2ea7011), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed ε, δ ∈ (0, 1/2), there are an integer s ≥ 1 and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to explicit unweighted simple bipartite Unique Games instances over Fs 2. If the formula is satisfiable the game has a labeling satisfying at least 1 − ε of its edges; if it is unsatisfiable every labeling satisfies at most δ of its edges. The edge set is nonempty and each constraint is a translation of the alphabet. The alphabet size and the polynomial’s degree and constants depend only on ε, δ.
